Maria (AE): Hey team — Customer X signed the MSA but is stuck on capacity sizing + pricing Qs. They want a short presales thread to confirm reserve vs burst costs and an autoscale fallback for AZ failover.

Jamal (Solutions): quick read — their traffic pattern: steady 120 rps with daily spikes to ~850 rps for 7-10m windows. Mostly chat completions, avg 60 tokens per request. Goal: p95 latency < 300ms and predictable monthly bill.

Priya (PSE): rough calc: steady load -> ~120 * 60 = 7200 tokens/sec. Peak -> 850 * 60 = 51k tokens/sec. With our current A10-equivalent throughput estimates (approx 6k tokens/sec per GPU at avg prompt size), sizing: steady -> 2 GPUs, peak -> ~9 GPUs. Will refine with actual model config.

Anna (SRE): important to call out cold-start window — if they rely on burst credits only, p95 will spike during coldstarts. Recommend reserved pool for base (2 GPUs) + burst credits / autoscale to 10 for spikes. Also AZ-aware preheat + KV cache warmup to reduce token work on spikes.

Customer-SRE: Can you translate that into expected monthly spend (reserved vs on-demand)? We need a number for procurement.

Kai (SalesOps): pricing note — reserved GPU month: $Xk/GPU/mo (committed), burst credits priced @ $Y/token-equivalent during sustained bursts. For quick comparison: base 2 reserved GPUs = $2*Xk = $Zk/mo. If they need avg 9 GPUs for 2h/day of spikes, incremental burst cost estimate ~ $Wk/mo. I'll put a simple calc.

Jamal (Solutions): sharing a tiny sketch (will run proper bench):

```
Scenario | GPUs reserved | avg additional burst hours/day | est monthly cost
Base steady | 2 | 0 | $Zk
Burst windows | 2 reserved + autoscale to 10 | 2h/day | $Zk + $Wk (~+35%)
Full-reserve (safety) | 10 reserved | 0 | ~$10*Xk
```

Priya (PSE): To be conservative on latency SLO, recommend: reserve 3 GPUs for base (small safety margin), autoscale to 11 for spikes, and enable preheat policy that keeps at least one warm node per AZ during expected windows. That lowers p95 tail on scale-outs.

Elena (Legal): FYI — Customer X's procurement requires a note that reserved capacity must be cancellable at 30d with a wind-down clause. Also they flagged an audit requirement: dedicated instances must be in VPC/private with KMS for keys. That pushes them towards Dedicated/Private offering (affects pricing).

Maria (AE): That legal constraint is the blocker. Customer prefers reserved for predictability, but legal wants private network + KMS. Can we offer Dedicated with reserved capacity and the same autoscale semantics?

Anna (SRE): Yes — Dedicated supports reserved pools + autoscale policy and VPC peering; pricing is higher due to isolation. Operational note: cross-AZ fallback will require reserves in 2 AZs or an explicit failover plan. If they need 99.9% latency at spikes, we must provision minimal hot capacity in both AZs.

Customer-SRE: What's the recommended minimal configuration to satisfy legal + latency without blowing the budget?

Priya (PSE): Suggested minimal for compliance + SLO: Dedicated reserved pool: 4 GPUs (spread 2/2 across AZs), autoscale to 12 for spikes, preheat windows around known traffic schedule, KV cache persistence enabled. Estimated cost: reserved 4 * Xk = $4Xk/mo + burst costs ~ $Vk/mo. This gives headroom for AZ failover and lowers cold-start tail.

Kai (SalesOps): I'll draft an option matrix for procurement: (A) Dedicated 4-reserve + autoscale to 12 + KMS (recommended), (B) Hosted base 3-reserve + burst credits + VPC peering (if legal accepts), (C) Full reserve 12 GPUs (if they want absolute isolation). Will include monthly cost ranges.

Maria (AE): Action items: Kai to produce option matrix & raw numbers by EOD, Priya to run a quick microbench on our 60-token chat workload and confirm tokens/sec per GPU by tomorrow, Anna to outline AZ failover runbook and preheat config, Elena to draft contractual language for 30d cancellation + KMS addendum. I'll share this with the customer after we have numbers.

Elena (Legal): note for contract: add clause that we will provide a failover plan and quarterly proof-of-performance reports for latency/p95 during spikes. Customer can request audit logs for KMS usage.

deploy-bot: Deployment check: dedicated-pool sizing template created in infra repo at https://repo.internal/inference/dedicated-templates#pool-4-az2

Customer-SRE: thanks — that's helpful. We'll review the option matrix. One question: can preheat be scheduled to minutes granularity or only hourly?

Anna (SRE): minutes granularity available for scheduled preheat via our Console API. We'll include example cron rules in the runbook.

Maria (AE): Great — thanks everyone. Kai, Priya, Anna, Elena: ping me when you have deliverables and I'll coordinate a 30m call with the customer's infra and procurement team. :thumbsup:
